kjv: when they offered before the LORD
mine: when they drew near before Yahweh
note: Hebrew beqorbatam, "in their drawing near"; the verb qarav can imply offering, but the text refers to their unauthorised approach (Lev 10:1-2) rather than naming an act of sacrifice.

kjv: the other lot for the scapegoat
note: Hebrew la'aza'zel, parallel to "for Yahweh", reads most naturally as a proper name (a wilderness being or place), not "goat that departs" (ez + azal) as the KJV, following the Vulgate caper emissarius, took it; also vv. 10, 26. Context: for Azazel (high confidence). The two lots are 'one for Yahweh and one for Azazel': the parallel requires a recipient, so Azazel is a name, as ESV, NRSV, NJPS and NET render it. What Azazel denotes (a wilderness being, a place, or 'removal') is left open by keeping the name. Other possible meanings: (1) 'for the scapegoat / the goat that departs' ('ez 'azal) — LXX to apopompaio, Vulgate caper emissarius, KJV, NIV, NASB; (2) 'for (complete) removal' — some lexicons (BDB); (3) a rugged cliff in the wilderness — Talmud (Yoma 67b), Rashi; (4) a demon or fallen angel — 1 Enoch 8-10, many modern scholars.

kjv: to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness
mine: to send it away into the wilderness to Azazel
note: Same term la'aza'zel; the goat is sent "to Azazel", the destination or recipient, rather than serving "as a scapegoat".
Hebrew te'annu et-naphshotekhem, "you shall humble/deny yourselves", understood as fasting and self-denial; "afflict your souls" suggests inner spiritual torment to a modern reader (also v. 31).
Hebrew shabbat shabbaton, an intensive "sabbath of sabbath-rest", i.e. a total cessation; the KJV reduces the emphatic doubling.
